approachQuestion.prompt:
Pair matching archive records

Input: arrays left and right of integer tags; duplicates are allowed. Return all index pairs [i,j] such that left[i]=right[j]. Each matching pair of positions appears exactly once; result order is arbitrary.

Example 1: left = [7,7,2], right = [7,2,7]. Output: [[0,0],[1,0],[2,1],[0,2],[1,2]] in any order. Example 2: left = [], right = [4]. Output: []. Both lengths are between 0 and 2,000. The result can be quadratic in input length; it must be materialized.

Constraints: input is immutable; all identifiers and numeric entries are signed 32-bit integers unless specified. Arithmetic uses signed 64-bit integers. Prefer the least expected running-time growth, then avoid unnecessary asymptotic auxiliary storage. Non-adversarial hashing of fixed-size integer keys/tuples has expected amortized constant cost.

options.text: Map each tag in the shorter input to all its original indices. Scan the longer input and emit a pair for every saved index under the current tag, orienting each pair as [leftIndex,rightIndex].
options.feedback: Every matching position pair is emitted at exactly one scanned position. Indexing the shorter side retains all necessary multiplicities with less working storage.

options.text: Comparison-sort copied (tag,index) records from both inputs and merge equal-tag runs, emitting the Cartesian product of their original indices.
options.feedback: Run products give the exact output, but sorting adds removable work when matches are sparse and requires copies of both inputs.

options.text: Map each tag from the shorter input to only one original index, then emit one pair per matching longer-side position.
options.feedback: left [7,7] and right [7] require two pairs. Keeping one index loses one of them.

options.text: Compare every left position with every right position and emit equal-tag pairs.
options.feedback: This is correct but brute force: even when no pair matches, it checks every cross-input combination rather than querying matching keys.

feedback.reason: Account for the unavoidable output size of a many-to-many key join and preserve every matching index.
details: Index the shorter input with tag-to-list-of-original-indices buckets. Scan the longer input, emitting one correctly oriented [leftIndex,rightIndex] for every index in its matching bucket. Keep the buckets until completion. If either input is empty return an empty result.

A tag appearing twice on the left and three times on the right creates six distinct index pairs. Retain every matching index and preserve left/right orientation even when the shorter indexed side changes.

Scan the longer input and emit a pair for every saved index under the current tag, orienting each pair as [leftIndex,rightIndex].”: Every matching position pair is emitted at exactly one scanned position. Indexing the shorter side retains all necessary multiplicities with less working storage.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Pair matching archive records — analyzed method”, n = left.length, m = right.length and r is the number of returned position pairs. List/output appends have amortized constant cost; copying one pair takes constant time. Choose its time and auxiliary-space pair. Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input for the stated size parameters, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.

options.text: Expected O(n + m + r + 1) time; O(min(n,m) + 1) auxiliary space.
Expected O(n + m + 1) time; O(min(n,m) + 1) space, independent of r.
Expected O(n + m + r + 1) time; O(r + 1) auxiliary space as the tight bound.

feedback.reason: Add unavoidable emitted-pair work to input scans and index storage.
details: Account for the unavoidable output size of a many-to-many key join and preserve every matching index.
Bucket construction and the outer scan cost expected O(n+m); bucket iterations total exactly r emitted pairs. Materialization adds O(r), hence expected O(n+m+r+1).
Buckets collectively retain exactly min(n,m) original indices and at most that many keys. The separate returned r pairs are excluded, giving O(min(n,m)+1).
“Expected O(n + m + r + 1) time; O(min(n,m) + 1) auxiliary space.”: Correct under the stated expected/amortized hashing model.
“Expected O(n + m + 1) time; O(min(n,m) + 1) space, independent of r.”: Materializing r pairs requires time proportional to r, which may be much larger than n+m.

“Expected O(n + m + r + 1) time; O(r + 1) auxiliary space as the tight bound.”: The returned pairs are excluded; working bucket storage depends on the smaller input and may be nonempty even when r is zero.
“O(nm + 1) time; O(1) auxiliary space.”: This describes nested comparisons, not the indexed join and its buckets.
